at starte på.explanation: "At starte på" means "to start on". To say you begin a task, put "på" (on) before the task: "Jeg starter på opgaven" (I start on the assignment). To say an engine or a machine starts, use "at starte" (to start) without "på": "Bilen starter ikke" (The car does not start).

at stave.explanation: "At stave" means "to spell". To ask someone how a word is spelled, use it with "man" (one): "Hvordan staver man det?" (How do you spell that?)

at stege.explanation: "At stege" means "to fry, to roast". To say you cook meat in a pan, say: "Jeg steger kød i panden" (I fry meat in the pan). To say you cook a duck in the oven, say: "Vi steger en and i ovnen" (We roast a duck in the oven). To cook in water, use "at koge" (to boil): "Jeg koger kartofler" (I boil potatoes).

at stemme.explanation: "At stemme" means "to vote". To say who you vote for, add "på" (on): "Jeg stemmer på ham" (I vote for him). To say a fact is correct, use the same verb: "Det stemmer!" (That is right!)

at stemme på.explanation: "At stemme på" means "to vote for". To name the person or party you choose, put it after "på" (on), where English says "for": "Vi stemte på Peter" (We voted for Peter).

at stige.explanation: "At stige" means "to rise / climb". To say a price goes up, say: "Prisen stiger" (The price is rising). To say you climb stairs, add "op ad" (up along): "Han stiger op ad trappen" (He climbs up the stairs). To say you get into a car, add "ind" (in): "Hun steg ind i bilen" (She got into the car).

at stige af.explanation: "At stige af" means "to get off". To say you leave a bus, a train or a bike, put "af" (off) after the verb: "Hun stiger af cyklen" (She gets off the bike). To say the opposite, use "at stige på" (to get on): "Jeg stiger på bussen" (I get on the bus).

at stige på.explanation: "At stige på" means "to get on". To say you board a bus, a train or a bike, put "på" (on) after the verb: "Vi stiger på toget i Odense" (We get on the train in Odense). To say the opposite, use "at stige af" (to get off): "Hun stiger af toget" (She gets off the train).

at stikke.explanation: "At stikke" means "to stick / sting". To say an insect stings you, say: "Bien stak mig" (The bee stung me). To say you push something into a place, add "i" (in): "Jeg stikker pengene i lommen" (I stick the money in my pocket).

at stikke af.explanation: "At stikke af" means "to run off". It is built from "at stikke" (to stick) and "af" (off). To tell what a thief did, say: "Tyven stak af" (The thief ran off).

at stikke en finger i jorden.explanation: "At stikke en finger i jorden" means "take stock". Literally, it is "to stick a finger in the ground".

at stikke en kæp i hjulet.explanation: "At stikke en kæp i hjulet" means "throw a wrench in the works". Literally, it is "to stick a stick in the wheel". To name the person whose plan you spoil, add "for" (for) and the person: "Jeg vil ikke stikke en kæp i hjulet for dig" (I do not want to spoil things for you).

at stille.explanation: "At stille" means "to put / place (upright)". To put something that stands, like a bottle, on a table, say: "Jeg stiller flasken på bordet" (I put the bottle on the table). To put something flat, like a book, use "at lægge" (to lay): "Jeg lægger bogen på bordet" (I put the book on the table).

at stille et spørgsmål.explanation: "At stille et spørgsmål" means "to ask a question". Literally, it is "to put a question". To ask a person directly, use "at spørge" (to ask): "Jeg vil spørge dig om noget" (I want to ask you something).

at stille op.explanation: "At stille op" means "to run (for office)". To say someone puts their name forward in an election, say: "Han stiller op for partiet" (He runs for the party). To say a team turns up to play, say: "Holdet stiller op til kampen" (The team turns out for the match). To say people line up, add "sig" (oneself): "Børnene stiller sig op i en række" (The children line up in a row).

at stille uret.explanation: "At stille uret" means "to set the clock". To say you move the clock ahead, add "en time frem" (an hour forward): "Vi stiller uret en time frem" (We set the clock an hour forward).

at stimulere.explanation: "At stimulere" means "to stimulate". To say you boost the economy, put "økonomien" (the economy) after it: "at stimulere økonomien" (to stimulate the economy).

at stirre.explanation: "At stirre" means "to stare". To name what you stare at, use "på" (at): "Hun stirrer på skærmen" (She stares at the screen). To say you stare into space, use "ud i luften" (out into the air): "Han stirrer ud i luften" (He stares into space).

at stjæle.explanation: "At stjæle" means "to steal". To say something was taken from you, say: "Nogen stjal min cykel" (Someone stole my bicycle). To say someone robbed a bank, use "at røve" (to rob): "Han røvede banken" (He robbed the bank).

at stole på.explanation: "At stole på" means "to trust". To say you trust someone, put "på" (on) before the person: "Jeg stoler på min læge" (I trust my doctor). In a sentence with "ikke" (not), "ikke" goes between the two words: "Jeg stoler ikke på ham" (I do not trust him).

at stoppe.explanation: "At stoppe" means "to stop". To say you quit doing something, add "med at" (with to) and a verb: "Jeg stopper med at spise slik" (I stop eating candy).

at straffe.explanation: "At straffe" means "to punish". To say what someone is punished for, add "for" (for): "Han blev straffet for sin fejl" (He was punished for his mistake).

at stramme.explanation: "At stramme" means "to tighten". To tighten a screw, say: "Jeg strammer skruen" (I tighten the screw). To say rules become stricter, say: "at stramme reglerne" (to make the rules stricter).

at streame.explanation: "At streame" means "to stream". The Danish verb is borrowed from the English word "stream".

at strejke.explanation: "At strejke" means "to strike", as in stopping work as a protest. To say the teachers are on strike, say: "Lærerne strejker" (The teachers are on strike). The noun is "strejke" (strike): "Der er strejke på skolen i dag" (There is a strike at the school today).
